requirement: Answer whether a customer has unpaid invoices without loading rows, list customers owing at least an amount exactly once each, and list customers with no invoices, rejecting a negative threshold.
skeleton: Customer and Invoice declarative models, has_unpaid selecting an exists() expression, customers_owing filtering customers by a correlated exists() with a threshold check, and customers_without_invoices filtering by a negated exists().
caption: Yes-or-no invoice questions answered with SQL EXISTS in SQLAlchemy instead of joins. Customer has an id and a name of up to 50 characters; Invoice has an id, a customer_id foreign key to customers, amount_cents and a paid flag defaulting to False. has_unpaid(session, customer_id) builds exists().where on the customer id and paid being false, selects it and returns bool of session.scalar, so the database answers without loading any invoice rows and the result is always a real bool. customers_owing(session, min_cents) raises ValueError saying min_cents must not be negative, then selects customer names where a correlated exists() finds an unpaid invoice for that customer with amount_cents at least min_cents, ordered by name; because EXISTS filters customers rather than multiplying them, a customer with several matching invoices appears once. customers_without_invoices(session) selects names where the negated exists() finds no invoice, ordered by name. The fixture asserts that has_unpaid is True for a customer with unpaid invoices and False for one whose only invoice is paid and one with none, that a zero threshold lists ann and cy once each, that the threshold is inclusive at 200 and excludes cy at 250, that -1 raises ValueError, and that only dee has no invoices.

plan.intent: Query invoice status without duplicate rows
constraints: has_unpaid returns a bool without loading invoice rows
Paid invoices never count as owed
Customers owing money are listed once each, ordered by name
Customers with no invoices are listed by name

rationale.teaches: exists() as a correlated semi-join filter, selected directly for booleans and negated with ~ for anti-joins.
rationale.why: A plain join multiplies parent rows by matching children and loading rows to test presence wastes work, and both look correct on data where every customer has at most one invoice.

ops.docstring: Answer yes-or-no questions about invoices with EXISTS instead of joins.

ops.stmt: from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, String, exists, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column

ops.source:
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    """Declarative base for the billing tables."""

class Invoice(Base):
    """One invoice for a customer, paid or not."""

    __tablename__ = "invoices"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    customer_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("customers.id"))
    amount_cents: Mapped[int]
    paid: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=False)

candidates.why_wrong: Joining invoices returns one row per matching invoice, so a customer with two unpaid invoices appears twice.
An invoice exactly equal to the threshold is excluded from the owing list.
Paid invoices count as unpaid, so a customer who settled everything is reported as owing.
The EXISTS test is not negated, so invoiced customers are returned instead of uninvoiced ones.
A threshold of zero is rejected although it is a valid minimum amount.
